parsed.explanation: No criminalization of trans identity and multiple protective statutes (safe spaces, women's, HIV, anti-bullying, local SOGI ordinances) are meaningful positives. However, documented exposures pull the score down: trans women housed in male jail dormitories with mandatory head-shaping and safety dependent on inmate hierarchies (tier-1 custody harm, though contingent on detention); service refusals with little legal consequence (tier-3, thin recourse); a documented pattern of transfemicide flagged by the national human rights commission (raw counts without denominators, but pattern language from an official body carries weight); police arrests of Pride participants; and local dress ordinances restricting gender expression (enforcement undocumented). The equality bill's 25-year failure signals weak national recourse. No universal-exposure facility ban or organized targeting campaign exists. Net: elevated risk with some working protections but insufficient remedy for documented harms.
